key_insight: Guidance for realistic human-object interaction animation can be induced from the diffusion denoising dynamics itself (diffusion forcing), removing the need for classifier-based or hand-crafted contact priors.
problem_solved: Generates realistic, contact-aware HOI animations by jointly modeling dynamic human motion and diverse object geometry without relying on manually designed contact priors or kinematic constraints.
method: Introduce LIGHT: a data-driven diffusion-forcing framework where useful guidance emerges from the denoising pace instead of external classifiers or hand-crafted priors.
Steer generation via the denoising schedule to encourage plausible contact formation and object-constrained motion trajectories.
Train end-to-end on paired human-object motion data so interaction-aware guidance is learned directly from examples.
impact: Reduces engineering overhead and brittle priors while improving contact quality and realism of HOI animations—beneficial for animation, AR/VR, simulation, and robot interaction tasks.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram of diffusion denoising showing how guidance emerges from the denoising pace (before vs after LIGHT).
Side-by-side qualitative comparison: prior methods (with hand-crafted priors) vs LIGHT illustrating contact quality and motion realism.
Architecture block diagram highlighting diffusion forcing, training data flow, and absence of classifier modules.
Bar/line chart of quantitative metrics (contact accuracy, realism scores) comparing LIGHT to baselines.
paper_title: Unleashing Guidance Without Classifiers for Human-Object Interaction Animation
paper_authors: Ziyin Wang, Sirui Xu, Chuan Guo, Bing Zhou, Jiangshan Gong
